title: Best AI Tools for Small Businesses
summary: We asked 150+ small business owners what the best AI tools were for their business. Here are the 21 that made the list.
body_markdown:
Instead of guessing which AI tools matter to small businesses, we asked them. More than 150 small business owners, founders, and operators told us, on the record, which AI tool actually changed how they work.


## Quick comparison: all 21 tools at a glance


List # Tool Best For


1 Claude + Claude Cowork Strategist, copywriter, and QA tester, including autonomous work via Cowork mode


2 ChatGPT Research, first drafts, and beating the blank page


3 Claude Code Letting a non-engineer on a lean team build and rebuild internal tools


4 Grammarly Cleaning up grammar, tone, and clarity in everyday business writing


5 Lava An AI "chief of staff" that connects tools you'd otherwise manage separately


6 Fathom Turning calls into a searchable record without anyone taking notes


7 Intercom Fin Consistent customer answers, day or night


8 Make Wiring the tools you already use together so a workflow runs itself


9 Gamma Turning a rough dataset or outline into a polished slide deck


10 Descript Video editing without a video background


11 Replit Building or rebuilding a website or app in plain language


12 Rella Social media scheduling with built-in AI performance insight


13 Memelord Catching a social trend the moment it starts accelerating


14 Warp Automated payroll, multi-state tax compliance, HRIS, and IT management


15 Rillet Automated reconciliations and close management


16 Fondo Bookkeeping, corporate tax filings, and tax credit identification


17 Ramp Expense assistant that drafts memos, fetches receipts, and auto-reviews low-risk spend


18 Brex Matches each expense & syncs the data directly to your accounting system


19 Fuku Sorting high-volume applications and candidate screening


20 Genstore.ai Running an entire e-commerce operation through one chat interface


21 Jobber Building and rebuilding field-service schedules automatically


## Research & writing for multiple use cases


### 1. Claude + Claude Cowork


**Best for:** acting as a strategist, copywriter, and QA tester for a founder wearing every hat, including autonomous work through Cowork mode.


**Pricing:** Free; Pro $17-20/month (Cowork included); Max from $100/month


Nigel, founder of[VendorLoop](https://getvendorloop.com/) , an SMS marketing platform for food truck operators, says Claude has become his "strategist, copywriter, QA tester, and thought partner" as a solo founder. But he's careful about where the actual value comes from: "AI is most valuable when you bring real domain expertise to the conversation. Claude doesn't know that. But when I pair its analytical horsepower with my understanding of how a tamale vendor in Austin actually runs their Saturday, the output is genuinely better than what I'd produce alone."


James Coombe, founder of[LLC Launch Kit](https://llclaunchkit.com/) , uses Claude's Cowork mode specifically for autonomous, scheduled work: it drafts and keeps his state-by-state compliance guides current on its own schedule, new state guides, FAQ updates, without him driving each update by hand. "I still approve anything before it goes live," he told us, "but the research, drafting, and fact-checking happen on their own schedule now." Most recently, it caught a stale figure before publishing: Texas had raised its franchise tax no-tax-due threshold for 2026, and an older draft still had the previous number.


### 2. ChatGPT


**Best for:** research, first drafts, and reducing the time between "I have no idea where to start" and something you can actually work with.


**Pricing:** Free; Plus $20/month; Pro $200/month


Michelle Shore, founder of[HarvestPak](https://harvestpak.com/) , uses ChatGPT for research she used to do the slow way. "Before, I would spend hours Googling and jumping between websites trying to piece everything together," she told us. "I'm a small business, so I can't hire someone every time I need help with something. ChatGPT has honestly let me do a lot of things myself that I probably would have had to pay someone else to do."


Bogdan Condurache, CPO and co-founder of[Brizy.io](https://www.brizy.io/) , uses it across the business, from turning rough product ideas into structured requirements to analyzing customer feedback. His filter for where it pays off: "Don’t start by asking 'Where can we replace people?' Start with 'Where are our people wasting time?' That's usually where AI creates the fastest ROI."


## Coding agents that build for you


### 3. Claude Code


**Best for:** letting a non-engineer on a lean team build and rebuild internal tools and processes.


Fırat Mıhcı, the solo founder and computational linguist behind[HumanizeMy.ai](https://humanizemy.ai/) , uses Codex alongside Claude Code to run research, product, and deployment as one coherent system. His statement of the human-in-the-loop principle is the clearest we heard across dozens of responses: "AI can generate an implementation, run a reproducible analysis, and prepare a rollback path. It cannot decide whether a research conclusion is justified, whether a customer's meaning survived a rewrite, or whether a public claim is honest. Keeping those decisions human is what turns the tool from a shortcut into infrastructure."


## Day-to-day operations


### 4. Grammarly


**Best for:** cleaning up grammar, tone, and clarity across business emails, proposals, and customer-facing communication.


**Pricing:** Free; Pro from around $12/month


Harrison Tang, CEO and co-founder of[Spokeo](https://www.spokeo.com/reverse-phone-lookup) , a people-search engine, told us communication tools are non-negotiable for a small team constantly in contact with customers and partners. "Grammarly is an AI-powered writing assistant that helps you improve your writing by correcting grammar, clarity, and quality," he said, pointing to small business emails, proposals, website content, and internal documentation as the places it earns its keep.


[Try Grammarly.](http://grammarly.com/)


### 5. Lava


**Best for:** an AI "chief of staff" that connects tools you'd otherwise manage separately.


James Colistra, founder of the podcast guesting agency[Wonderfish](https://wonderfish.xyz/) , uses Lava to run more than a dozen workflows across Slack, Gmail, and HubSpot. "Every connected tool becomes more valuable because the AI agent can orchestrate them together behind the scenes," he said, instead of requiring him to create and manage a separate account for every service he connects to.


[Check out Lava here.](https://www.lava.so/)


## Notetaker for Meetings + Calls


### 6. Fathom


**Best for:** turning calls and interviews into a searchable, shareable record without anyone taking notes.


**Pricing:** Free forever tier; Premium $20/month


Jafar Sadhik, Growth Marketing Expert at[Atoa Payments](https://paywithatoa.co.uk/) , uses Fathom to record meetings, create searchable transcripts, and produce summaries with decisions and action items. "Its biggest impact is allowing us to concentrate fully on conversations instead of taking notes," he said, though his team still reviews summaries before relying on them, "particularly when a discussion includes technical or financial details."


Ivan Vislavskiy, CEO and co-founder of[Comrade Digital Marketing Agency](https://comradeweb.com/) , echoed the same result: "every action item and decision is captured and easily searchable," which has saved his team real hours each week on writing up notes and following up.


[Check out Fathom](https://www.fathom.ai/) .


## Customer Support


### 7. Intercom Fin


**Best for:** consistent customer answers around the clock without adding headcount to the support queue.


Kristiyan Yankov, co-founder of[Above Apex](https://aboveapex.com/) , picked Intercom Fin because "customer response time is one of the easiest places for a small team to lose potential revenue." What he values isn't automation for its own sake, it's consistency: "customers should receive the same accurate answer whether they contact you at 10 AM or 10 PM." He measures the tool by three things: how many questions it resolves without a human, whether satisfaction holds up, and how much time it hands back to the team.


[Explore Fin.](https://fin.ai/)


## Connecting your toolstack


### 8. Make


**Best for:** connecting the apps a small business already runs on so a workflow executes itself, without adding headcount.


**Pricing:** Free; Core from $12/month; Pro from $21/month; Teams from $38/month


Daniel Battaglia, Founder of[Parksy](http://parksy.com/) , wired Make.com to OpenAI to solve a volume problem: new listings arrive with patchy detail because people write them on their phone in thirty seconds. "The workflow reads each one, flags what's missing, drafts a cleaner description for the host to approve, and files it into the right location page," he said.


[Start using Make.](http://www.make.com/)


## Marketing + Sales


### 9. Gamma


**Best for:** turning a rough dataset or outline into a polished slide deck in minutes.


**Pricing:** Free tier


Vamsi Nellutla, President of[Dallas Data Science Academy](https://dallasdatascienceacademy.ai/) , feeds Gamma the findings from a small dataset and lets it handle the layout. "It lets me spend my energy on the part that actually matters: the ideas and the story the data is telling, not nudging text boxes into alignment," he said. "For a small operation like mine, where I'm the analyst and the presenter and everything in between, that shift is the difference between a rushed deck and one a board takes seriously."


[Try Gamma.](https://gamma.app/)


### 10. Descript


**Best for:** video editing without a video background.


**Pricing:** Free; Hobbyist $16/month; Creator $24/month; Business $50/month


[Molly McClure,](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mollysmcclure/) a marketing leader for small businesses, calls Descript her "go-to for video editing." "I can simply ask it to make edits that are beyond my technical skill set, which saves a tremendous amount of time," she said.


[Check out Descript.](https://www.descript.com/)


### 11. Replit


**Best for:** building or rebuilding a website or app by describing what you want in plain language.


**Pricing:** Free (Starter); Core $17-20/month; Pro $95-100/month


Aaron Traub, owner of[Geaux SEO](https://geauxseo.com/) , moved his own business website from WordPress to one he built with Replit, and now does the same for clients. "I can build new pages, test ideas, make changes, and add new features much faster than I could before," he said.


[Check out Replit.](https://replit.com/)


### 12. Rella


**Best for:** scheduling social content with a built-in AI assistant that surfaces what's actually resonating.


**Pricing:** Free trial, Pro $24/month; Premium $48/month; Premium Plus $64/month


Erin Hoy, founder of[Her Digital Legacy](https://herdigitallegacy.com/) , pointed to Rella's integrated AI assistant, "Ella." She highlighted two features in particular: advanced analytics for prompting deep dives into performance data, and actionable insights that make it easy to "identify and duplicate what is resonating with your audience."


[Explore Rella.](https://getrella.com/)


### 13. Memelord


**Best for:** catching a social trend the moment it starts accelerating instead of after everyone's already seen it.


Jason Levin, CEO and founder of Memelord, built the platform's own AI trend-detection alerts to solve a speed problem for his four-person marketing team. "The software pings us the second a meme starts accelerating, so we jump on a trend before it peaks instead of posting the joke everyone already saw," he said. "It turned trend-spotting from a gut feeling into a repeatable system."


[Check out Memelord.](http://memelord.com/)


## Back office: finance, bookkeeping, payroll and taxes


### 14. Warp


**Best for:** automated payroll, multi-state tax compliance, and employee onboarding & offboarding.


**Pricing:** Starting at $35/employee


"Warp gives me peace of mind – I don't have to worry about compliance or tax notices. I've gotten back so much time from payroll headaches,” said Rahul Sonwalkar, Founder of[Julius AI](https://julius.ai/) .


[Explore Warp for Small Businesses.](https://www.warp.co/small-business)


### 15. Rillet


**Best for:** real-time general ledger, accounting agents, automated reconciliations, and close management.


Ben Hudson, a controller at[Highway](https://highway.com/) , said: "We set up a weekly workflow in Rillet’s Aura AI to perform our aging analyses and craft customer emails for past-due items. What used to be an entire morning of manual work is now fully automated. We can run a smaller team in perpetuity because of Rillet's flexibility and speed. You don't need to be an expert in ERPs to figure out how to use it."


[Check out Rillet.](https://www.rillet.com/)


### 16. Fondo


**Best for:** automating bookkeeping, corporate tax filings, and tax credit identification.


Sky Yang, Co-Founder and CEO of[Imagine AI](https://imagine.ai/) , said: "We were thinking of hiring a financial analyst and an accountant, but Fondo took care of everything."


[Explore Fondo.](https://fondo.com/)


### 17. Ramp


**Best for:** an AI expense assistant that drafts memos, fetches receipts, and auto-reviews low-risk spend.


“Ramp gives you things that most companies of our size wouldn’t get. All told, Ramp has saved Roof Squad upwards of 50 hours a week across expense management, AP, and treasury,” said Alejandro Calderon at Roof Squad.


[Learn more about Ramp here.](https://ramp.com/)


### 18. Brex


**Best for:** matching each expense to its corresponding corporate card transaction and syncing the data directly to your accounting system.


Backburner Labs’ collapsed month-end reconciliation from 30 hours to less than 3 hours. “Brex knocked it out of the park with the AI automation on the accounting module and the custom integration with Xero,” said Parker Schlank, CFO at[Backburner Labs](https://www.backburnerlabs.io/) .


[Check out Brex here.](https://www.brex.com/)


## Role & Industry Specific Tools


### 19. Fuku.ai: for recruiting


**Best for:** sorting high volume, like candidate screening, without losing the judgment that matters most.


Irina Duisimbekova, Founder of[SympathiQ](https://www.sympathiq.com/) , said they use Fuku.AI's "Fiona" as an AI interviewer that conducts independent video screening interviews with every specialist who joins the platform. "Prior to Fiona, our little group was making initial screening calls for hours," they told us. "Now she's on the first round, and we can concentrate on the other candidates that are best suited. It has streamlined our process and made it more scalable, which is crucial for a lean team such as ours."


[Check out Fuku.ai.](http://fuku.ai/)


### 20. Genstore: for e-commerce


**Best for:** running the entire operational side of a DTC store, research, listings, inventory, and marketing, through one chat interface.


**Pricing:** Free; Lite $25/month; Growth $75/month


Moshe Oestreicher, CEO of[Perroquet Shoes](https://perroquetshoes.com/) , used to spend multiple hours a week on product research, listing creation, and inventory management. "I can literally describe a new shoe concept in natural language, and the AI curates drop-shipping options, generates complete product listings, and even sets up marketing campaigns," he said. "So far it's saved us roughly 30-50 hours per week in operational work."


[Explore Genstore.ai.](http://genstore.ai/)


### 21. Jobber: for in-person service providers


**Best for:** building and rebuilding field-service schedules automatically as jobs change.


**Pricing:** Core $49/month


Sofia Martinez, CEO of[Sparkly Maid Austin](https://sparklymaidaustin.com/) , says Jobber is the tool that's changed the most for her business: it creates daily schedules, factors in drive time between job sites, and rearranges everything automatically when a cancellation comes in. "This is the part that I was most surprised by," she said. "The time savings on scheduling were not the real win. It was the drive time we no longer wasted; a system routing by geography does it better than I ever did guessing by memory."


[Check out Jobber.](https://www.getjobber.com/)


## How to choose your AI tool


Based on what worked (and didn't) across the submissions we received, a simple filter emerges:


1. **Name the bottleneck first, not the tool.** Where do you or your team lose the most hours to repetitive, low-judgment work?
2. **Decide what still needs a human before you turn it on.** For customer-facing replies, financial transactions, and anything regulatory, keep a person in the approval loop from day one.
3. **Judge it by time and errors given back, not activity generated.** Several respondents warned against measuring AI success by message volume or documents produced. The better measure is hours returned to the team and mistakes caught before they became expensive.


## Frequently asked questions


### **What is the most popular AI tool small business owners actually use?**


Across our responses, ChatGPT and Claude were named most often, mainly for research, first drafts, and reducing "blank page" time on writing and planning tasks. Claude Code came up nearly as often, especially among non-technical founders using it to build internal tools without hiring an engineer.


### **Are AI tools actually worth it for a small business?**


Based on the specific, numbers-backed responses we collected, yes, when the tool is aimed at a defined bottleneck. Examples ranged from cutting certain tasks from two days to 40 minutes and giving back 30-50 hours a week of operational work.


### **What's the best free AI tool for a small business?**


ChatGPT's free tier and Claude's free tier cover the research, drafting, and brainstorming use cases most respondents described.
